request: Replace continuous settings scroll with separate pages
title: Separate settings into individual pages
purpose: Display only the selected settings category

files.purpose: Make each settings category an isolated page.
files.previous_behavior: All settings sections shared one continuous scroller; scrolling changed the highlighted category.
files.new_behavior: Only the selected section is visible. Category clicks commit text, clear search and reset scroll. Search filters categories while showing a single matching page; scrolling cannot change category.
files.data_impact: none: UI visibility changes only; existing settings persistence is unchanged.
files.access_control_impact: none: no authentication or permission changes.
risks: Search automatically switches to the first matching page when the current page does not match.
files.rollback: Revert this commit and rebuild; all saved settings remain compatible.

production_safety.operational_data: No operational settings or profile data read or modified; automated browser tests used synthetic data.
external_side_effects: Local build in native/publish-settings-pages; desktop shortcut updated to this build; running Oinzi unchanged.

verification.evidence: All 12 settings categories show exactly one page, scrolling preserves selection, search remains single-page and category clicks clear search. Compact header and drag regression checks also passed without page errors.

verification.command: dotnet publish native/native.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o native/publish-settings-pages -p:NoWarn=MSB3277 -v quiet

residual_risks: Live user settings data was not used in tests; each category resets its scroll position when selected.
